meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You will not withstand a blow from a coconut.
Why did you do that just now?
How foolish you are!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What kind of total nonsense is this?
Now we will think of something, Chef.
Timur, what have you done here?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Timur, what have you done here?
And what are you doing here?
It seems we did not get caught here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'make, cause'.

examples.trans: Timur, what have you done here?
What have you done right now, Fedya?
What have you done, Victoria?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'brother' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Brother, just do not worry!
Chef, do not throw the bottle away.
There is no need to throw him off the roof.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Just do not worry.
Brother, just do not worry!
Yes, just do not tell anyone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.
You must not be overfed right now.
Yes, it is just so unexpected.

переживать.gloss: to worry, to fret; to go through

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'живать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry, to fret; to go through', paired with 'пережить'.

examples.trans: Brother, just do not worry!
Why are you worrying like that?
Don't worry, everything will be fine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'his', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It overshadowed that unpleasant incident.
Of course, you are completely free.
What kind of report will he write now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ильно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I did not hit him very hard.
The hotel guests are complaining about loud noise.
I love you very much.

meanings.en: to knock down, to hit, to strike
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'бить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'knock down, hit, strike down', paired with 'сбивать'.

examples.trans: I did not hit him very hard.
The driver knocked down a road sign.

examples.text: Нет. Вы сбили светофор на дороге!
examples.trans: No. You knocked down a traffic light on the road!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Yes, it is just so unexpected.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'жасный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('terrible').

examples.trans: This is simply a terrible hotel!
What a horrible person you are!
It's a terrible flat.

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common feminine noun meaning 'hotel' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is simply a terrible hotel!

examples.text: Ладно, поезжай в гостиницу, ты устала.
examples.trans: Alright, go to the hotel, you're tired.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: After you, it is very close by.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: He hanged himself out of jealousy.
Everything's fine.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: He wanted to speak with the chef.
I want coffee.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'бить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to kill', paired with 'убивать'.

examples.trans: Please do not kill me.
Everyone here wants to kill me.
You nearly killed me.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'miracle' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It is a miracle that I stayed alive.
This is a culinary miracle!

examples.text: Потому что это настоящее кулинарное чудо!
examples.trans: Because it is a real culinary miracle!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'remained', paired with 'оставаться'.

examples.trans: There's nothing left.
I'll stay at home.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('alive').

examples.trans: Well, I am completely alive.
Brother, just do not worry!

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'лагать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning '(I) suggest', paired with 'предложить'.

examples.trans: I suggest writing a good review.
What do you suggest?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'писать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'write', paired with 'писать'.

examples.trans: I suggest writing a good review.
